claims.value: 4 sources: THP-1 DMSO SILAC light anti-LSD1 IP (rows 1-10), THP-1 OG86 SILAC heavy anti-LSD1 IP (rows 11-20), THP-1 DMSO SILAC light IgG control IP (rows 21-30), THP-1 OG86 SILAC heavy IgG control IP (rows 31-40)
claims.evidence: Channel map: supp Methods 'Heavy-labeled cells were exposed to 250nM of OG86 and the light-labeled to DMSO control for 48 hours ... The lysates from heavy-OG86 or light-DMSO were combined and incubated with the anti-LSD1 or anti-IgG rabbit antibodies'; paper Results 'cells were grown in heavy or light media ... treated with OG86 250 nM or DMSO vehicle respectively'. Data check: txt2 proteinGroups KDM1A Intensity L 351800000 / H 192530000 and HMG20B 13691000 / 3929200, GSE1 84065000 / 26076000, RREB1 15370000 / 4426000 are exactly the 'Intensity DMSO' / 'Intensity OG86' columns of Table S1, so L = DMSO and H = OG86; raw KDM1A H/L 0.56 matches the supp statement 'ratio ... heavy-OG86 vs light-DMSO ... for KDM1A itself was 0.55'; HMG20B normalized H/L 0.47 (reduced, as reported). The anti-LSD1 and IgG pull-downs are two physical pull-downs of the same combined lysate, so each (pull-down, channel) gets its own source name; the DMSO light channel of the LSD1 IP and of the IgG IP come from the same light culture (likewise heavy). txt.zip contains only IgG_* raw files and txt2.zip only LSD1_* raw files; both summary.txt Multiplicity 2, Labels1 Arg6;Lys8.

One SILAC experiment: one heavy (OG86) and one light (DMSO) culture, 40 million cells per condition, lysates combined and split into anti-LSD1 and IgG pull-downs. Each factor-value group (immunoprecipitation x treatment) contains exactly one culture, so 1 in every group (README.adoc:330; campaign rule 3). No replicate experiment is deposited or described.

limitations: Supp Methods says cells were grown in 'heavy methionine and arginine' medium; the deposited MaxQuant searches use Arg6;Lys8 (and Lys8-labelled pairs are present in evidence.txt). The search configuration is annotated; the 'methionine' wording is treated as a typo.

Two searched raw files are not deposited: 2014_1204_Alba_LSD1_4.raw and 2014_1204_Alba_IgG_3.raw appear in summary.txt but not in the PRIDE file list. The SDRF covers the 20 deposited raws; fraction identifiers keep the slice number from the file name, so fraction 4 (LSD1) and 3 (IgG) are absent.
Supp says each gel lane was cut into 10 pieces, but 11 files per lane were searched (numbered 1-11). Slice numbers are taken from file names.

The PRIDE data processing protocol (Mascot 2.6.0, 10 ppm / 0.60 Da) and sample protocol ('Nuclear extraction') describe the label-free nuclear IP-MS (Orbitrap Fusion, Tables S2/S3), whose files are not in this deposit. The deposited SILAC data were searched with MaxQuant 1.5.1.2, so the SDRF uses the MaxQuant settings.
Precursor mass tolerance is 'not available': no mqpar.xml is deposited, and parameters.txt/summary.txt record only MS/MS tolerances. Because of this, convert-openms exits 1.

Reduction and alkylation reagents are 'not available': the lysis buffer contains 1 mM DTT, but no in-gel reduction/alkylation step is described. Carbamidomethyl (C) is a fixed search modification only.

The culture medium is RPMI 1640 from the general THP1 culture statement. The SILAC medium base is not named separately. Passage number is 'not available'; the 15 days / 7 passages of labelling are not an absolute passage number. Cell type is 'not available' because none is stated.
OG86 has no ontology term (free text). Its concentration and duration (250 nM, 48 h) are recorded here only.
Single SILAC experiment without biological replication; biological replicate is 1 in each group.
The review is handed off to an external sdrf-adversarial-review (REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL); not self-approved.
